prompt: Write a blog post in three fixed steps: create an outline, check it covers the brief, then write the full draft from the outline.
tells: then write the full draft from the outline
why: Known steps in a known order, each feeding the next, with a check in between.
trap: An agent loop is for when you don't know the steps; here you do.

prompt: Marketing copy is always generated in English first, then translated into Spanish, then checked against a glossary.
tells: generated in English first, then translated
why: A fixed pipeline of LLM calls; easier to debug and test than an agent.
trap: Each step needs the previous output, so they can't run in parallel.

prompt: For each contract: first extract the key clauses, then validate the extraction with code, then summarize only the clauses that passed.
tells: then validate the extraction with code
why: Splitting into fixed calls with a programmatic gate makes each easier and more reliable.
trap: Nothing is decided at run time; the steps are always the same.

prompt: A compliance team wants every report produced the same predictable way, auditable step by step, and never improvised.
why: A workflow with fixed steps is predictable and auditable; an agent chooses its own path.
trap: Agents add flexibility, which is exactly what this team doesn't want.
